A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LPGW research, with matching methods, experiments, and extensive proofs. Their readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison despite reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original distance-approximation, shape-retrieval, noisy-digit classification, and interpolation results in Section 4 and Appendices I–K.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and results, and adds a clean/noisy digit-reconstruction comparison in Section 4.3.

M1.justification: The operational LPGW embedding, PGW transport-plan computation, barycentric projection, and discrete discrepancy remain unchanged; compare v1 Equation (23) with v3 Equation (25). Appendix C adds a formal treatment of non-Monge embeddings without establishing a changed numerical procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use elliptical disks, 2D shapes, complete/incomplete 3D shapes, and rotated/noisy MNIST point clouds. Digit interpolation and endpoint reconstruction already appear in v1 Appendix K.1; v3's additional reconstruction illustration stays within this coverage.

E2.justification: The empirical comparator sets remain unchanged: PGW for disks, GW/PGW/LGW for shape retrieval, and LOT/LGW for embedding classification. The new reconstruction illustration reuses the embedding comparators. Appendix M.2 adds complexity and approximate-cost comparisons, without documenting additional classifier evaluations.

E3.justification: The added reconstruction comparison uses clean digits and noise mass η = 0.2, introducing a limited additional evaluation setting. The protocols supporting Tables 1–4 retain their splits, preprocessing, metrics, classifiers, and parameter settings.

E4.justification: v3 Figure 1b adds a direct clean/noisy reconstruction comparison to examine whether embeddings retain noise. Existing reference-space and λ sensitivity analyses, nearest-neighbor confusion matrices, t-SNE plots, and interpolation examples remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report ten-fold classification averages and 10,000 randomized representative-selection iterations for nearest-neighbor analysis. Neither adds seed information, confidence intervals, dispersion estimates, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Every numerical entry in Tables 1–4 is unchanged. v3 adds reconstruction results showing noise exclusion by LPGW, and Appendix M.2 states approximate costs of 50 hours for OT and 400 hours for GW/PGW versus 3–5 minutes for linear embeddings. The measurement basis of these additional runtime statements is unspecified.

T1.justification: Appendix C adds conditional-distribution embedding definitions and derivations, and Appendix H.4 supplies a short proof of Proposition 3.3. v3 also corrects the main LPGW mass-penalty sign and partial-plan domain, revises the measure-minimum definition, and adds or changes complexity expressions. The core propositions and lengthy existing proofs are largely retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims: LPGW linearizes PGW, has metric properties under assumptions, reduces pairwise transport solves from quadratic to linear in the number of spaces, and preserves useful partial matching.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 explicitly connects reconstructed noise exclusion to classification robustness. New Appendices J and M.2 discuss the distinction between theoretical distances and practical approximations, and the computational obstacle to full-transport classifier comparisons. Existing approximation-error and reference-selection limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-repository link in the abstract and supplies the GW barycenter objective missing from v1 Equation (100). Hardware, established hyperparameters, and existing experiment implementation details remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Zhang et al., Cycle Consistent Probability Divergences Across Different Spaces, to the introduction's related-work citations. The positioning relative to LOT, LGW, and PGW remains unchanged; other reference renumbering and bibliographic updates do not introduce new works.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most prose remain intact. v3 makes localized wording and grammar edits, regroups contribution bullets, and adds focused appendix explanations and an acknowledgment.

P2.justification: v3 combines the MNIST illustration with a new reconstruction panel, adds complexity Table 5, and relocates the pairwise-distance figure from the main text to Appendix L. Page geometry, figure sizes, and table placement change, while most existing graphical content and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The code link, completed interpolation objective, and reconstruction evidence improve documentation and explanation. However, new technical material introduces unresolved inconsistencies: Equation (45) subtracts an embedding from itself, and Equation (46) changes a multiplicative complexity factor into an additive term without explanation. With benchmark results unchanged, these competing effects prevent a confident judgment of net overall improvement.
